text: Let the circle $C_{1}:x^{2}+y^{2}-2(x+y)+1=0$ and $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ be a circle having centre at $(-1,0)$ and radius 2 . sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} C_{1}:x^{2}+y^{2}-2(x+y)+1=0 \\ C_{2}:(x+1)^{2}+y^{2}=(2)^{2} \\ x^{2}+y^{2}+2x-3=0 \end{array}$

Common chord is

$\begin{array}{l} C_{1}-C_{2}=0 \\ \Rightarrow 2x+y-2=0 \end{array}$

also, this line intersects the $y$-axis at the point

$\begin{array}{l} P(0,y). \\ \Rightarrow y=2 \end{array}$

$P(0,2)$

Distance of point $P$ from $(1,1)$ is

$\begin{array}{l} d=\sqrt{(0-1)^{2}+(2-1)^{2}} \\ =\sqrt{1^{2}+1^{2}} \\ d=\sqrt{2} \\ \Rightarrow d^{2}=2 \end{array}$

solution.body:

Squaring,

text: Let $⃗{a}=2\hat{i}+5\hat{j}-\hat{k},⃗{b}=2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ and $⃗{c}$ be three vectors such that $(⃗{c}+\hat{i})\times (⃗{a}+⃗{b}+\hat{i})=⃗{a}\times (⃗{c}+\hat{i})$. If $⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}=-29$, then $⃗{c}\cdot (-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $⃗{a}\times (⃗{c}+\hat{i})=-(⃗{c}+\hat{i})\times ⃗{a}$, the given relation becomes

$(⃗{c}+\hat{i})\times (⃗{a}+⃗{b}+\hat{i})+(⃗{c}+\hat{i})\times ⃗{a}=⃗{0}\Rightarrow (⃗{c}+\hat{i})\times (2⃗{a}+⃗{b}+\hat{i})=⃗{0}$

$2⃗{a}+⃗{b}+\hat{i}=(4+2+1)\hat{i}+(10-2)\hat{j}+(-2+2)\hat{k}=7\hat{i}+8\hat{j}$.

So $⃗{c}+\hat{i}=λ(7\hat{i}+8\hat{j})$, i.e. $⃗{c}=(7λ-1)\hat{i}+8λ\hat{j}$.

$⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}=2(7λ-1)+5(8λ)=54λ-2=-29\Rightarrow λ=-\dfrac{1}{2}$

Thus $⃗{c}=-\dfrac{9}{2}\hat{i}-4\hat{j}$ and

$⃗{c}\cdot (-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})=9-4+0=5$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: If $y(θ)=\frac{2\cos θ+\cos 2θ}{\cos 3θ+4\cos 2θ+5\cos θ+2}$, then at $θ=\frac{π}{2},y^{''}+y^{'}+y$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} y(θ)=\dfrac{2\cos θ+\cos 2θ}{\cos 3θ+4\cos 2θ+5\cos θ+2} \\ =\dfrac{2\cos ^{2}θ+2\cos θ-1}{4\cos ^{3}θ+8\cos ^{2}θ+2\cos θ-2} \\ =\dfrac{2\cos ^{2}θ+2\cos θ-1}{(2\cos ^{2}θ+2\cos θ-1)(2\cos θ+2)} \\ =\dfrac{1}{2(1+\cos θ)}=\dfrac{1}{4\cos ^{2}θ/2}=\dfrac{\sec ^{2}θ/2}{4} \\ y^{'}(θ)=\dfrac{1}{4}\left (2\sec \dfrac{θ}{2}\cdot \sec \dfrac{θ}{2}\cdot \tan \dfrac{θ}{2}\cdot \dfrac{1}{2}\right ) \\ =\dfrac{1}{4}\sec ^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}\cdot \tan \dfrac{θ}{2} \end{array}$

$y^{''}(θ)=\frac{1}{4}\left (\tan \frac{θ}{2}\right )\left (\sec ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}\cdot \tan \frac{θ}{2}\right )+\frac{1}{4}\sec ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}\cdot \sec ^{2}\frac{θ}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{at}θ=\dfrac{π}{2},y(θ)=\dfrac{1}{2},y^{'}(θ)=\dfrac{1}{2},y^{''}(θ)=1 \\ \therefore \quad y+y^{'}+y^{''}=2 \end{array}$

text: Let $β(\mathrm{m},\mathrm{n})=\int\limits _{0}^{1}x^{\mathrm{m}-1}(1-x)^{\mathrm{n}-1}\mathrm{d}x,\mathrm{m},\mathrm{n}>0$. If $\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left (1-x^{10}\right )^{20}\mathrm{d}x=\mathrm{a}\times β(\mathrm{b},\mathrm{c})$, then $100(\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+\mathrm{c})$ equals $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
First, let's rewrite the given integral using the given form of the Beta function. The given integral is:

$\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left (1-x^{10}\right )^{20}\mathrm{d}x$

To use the Beta function, let us make a substitution. Let $x^{10}=t$. Then, $dx=\frac{1}{10}t^{-\frac{9}{10}}dt$ or $dx=\frac{1}{10}t^{-\frac{9}{10}}dt$. The limits of integration change as follows: when $x=0$, $t=0$, and when $x=1$, $t=1$.

Substituting these into the integral, we have:

$\int\limits _{0}^{1}(1-t)^{20}\cdot \frac{1}{10}t^{-\frac{9}{10}}dt$

which simplifies to:

$\frac{1}{10}\int\limits _{0}^{1}(1-t)^{20}t^{-\frac{9}{10}}dt$

We recognize this integral as a Beta function $β(m,n)$ where $m=1-\frac{9}{10}=\frac{1}{10}$ and $n=20+1=21$.

Therefore, we can write this as:

$\frac{1}{10}β\left (\frac{1}{10},21\right )$

Comparing this to $a\times β(b,c)$, we have $a=\frac{1}{10}$, $b=\frac{1}{10}$, and $c=21$.

Now we calculate $100(a+b+c)$:

$100\left (\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{10}+21\right )=100\left (\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{10}+21\right )=100\left (\frac{1}{5}+21\right )=100\left (\frac{1}{5}+\frac{105}{5}\right )=100\left (\frac{106}{5}\right )=100\times 21.2=2120$

So, the answer is Option D, 2120.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift

text: The coefficients $\mathrm{a},\mathrm{b},\mathrm{c}$ in the quadratic equation $\mathrm{a}x^{2}+\mathrm{bx}+\mathrm{c}=0$ are from the set $\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$. If the probability of this equation having one real root bigger than the other is p, then 216p equals :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Each of $a$, $b$, $c$ can be any of the 6 numbers independently, so there are $6^{3}=216$ equally likely equations.

One real root is bigger than the other exactly when the roots are real and distinct, i.e. $b^{2}>4ac$, i.e. $ac<\dfrac{b^{2}}{4}$.

$b=1$ or $b=2$: this needs $ac<1$, impossible since $ac\geq 1$; no case.

$b=3$: $ac<2.25$, so $ac\in \{1,2\}$: $(a,c)=(1,1),(1,2),(2,1)$; 3 cases.

$b=4$: $ac<4$, so $ac\in \{1,2,3\}$: the 3 pairs above and $(1,3),(3,1)$; 5 cases.

$b=5$: $ac\leq 6$: $ac=1$ gives 1 pair, $ac=2$ gives 2, $ac=3$ gives 2, $ac=4$ gives $(1,4),(4,1),(2,2)$, $ac=5$ gives 2, $ac=6$ gives $(1,6),(6,1),(2,3),(3,2)$; $1+2+2+3+2+4=14$ cases.

$b=6$: $ac<9$, so $ac\leq 8$: the 14 pairs above and $(2,4),(4,2)$ for $ac=8$ ($ac=7$ is impossible); 16 cases.

Favourable cases $=3+5+14+16=38$, so $p=\dfrac{38}{216}$ and $216p=38$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift

text: Let $αβ\neq 0$ and $A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} β & α & 3 \\ α & α & β \\ -β & α & 2α \end{array}\right ]$. If $B=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 3α & -9 & 3α \\ -α & 7 & -2α \\ -2α & 5 & -2β \end{array}\right ]$ is the matrix of cofactors of the elements of $A$, then $\det (AB)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} β & α & 3 \\ α & α & β \\ -β & α & 2α \end{array}\right ],B=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 3α & -9 & 3α \\ -α & 7 & -2α \\ -2α & 5 & -2β \end{array}\right ]$

Cofactor of $A$-matrix is

$=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 2α^{2}-αβ & -\left (2α^{2}+β^{2}\right ) & α^{2}+αβ \\ -\left (2α^{2}-3α\right ) & (2αβ+3β) & -(2αβ) \\ αβ-3α & -\left (β^{2}-3α\right ) & βα-α^{2} \end{array}\right ]$

which is equal to matrix $B$

So, by comparing elements of two matrix

$\begin{array}{lllllll} \Rightarrow αβ-3α=-2α \\ \Rightarrow αβ-α=0 \\ \Rightarrow α(β-1)=0 \\ \Rightarrow α=0\text{or}β=1[\because α\text{cannot be}0] \\ \Rightarrow β=1 \\ \text{and}-β^{2}+3α=5 \\ \Rightarrow 3α=6 \\ \Rightarrow α=2 \\ A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & 4 \end{array}\right ] \\ \mathrm{Det}(AB)=|A||B|=|A|\left |(\mathrm{adj}A)^{⊤}\right | \\ =|A|\cdot |A|^{2} \\ =|A|^{3} \\ =(6-18+18)^{3} \\ =6^{3} \\ =216 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift

text: For $x⩾0$, the least value of $\mathrm{K}$, for which $4^{1+x}+4^{1-x},\frac{\mathrm{K}}{2},16^{x}+16^{-x}$ are three consecutive terms of an A.P., is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In an A.P. the middle term is the mean of its neighbours, so

$K=4^{1+x}+4^{1-x}+16^{x}+16^{-x}$

Let $t=4^{x}$; for $x\geq 0$, $t\geq 1$. Then $K=4\left (t+\dfrac{1}{t}\right )+t^{2}+\dfrac{1}{t^{2}}$.

With $u=t+\dfrac{1}{t}$, $t^{2}+\dfrac{1}{t^{2}}=u^{2}-2$, so $K=u^{2}+4u-2=(u+2)^{2}-6$.

For $t\geq 1$, $u=t+\dfrac{1}{t}\geq 2$, with equality at $t=1$, i.e. $x=0$. As $(u+2)^{2}-6$ increases for $u\geq 2$, the least value is $K=4^{2}-6=10$.

The A.M.-G.M. bound $K\geq 4\sqrt{4 16}=8$ is never reached, because its four terms are never equal (at $x=0$ they are $4,4,1,1$).

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift

solution.body:

For $x<0$: $y=-x^{2}$ and $y=2x$; $-x^{2}=2x$ gives $x=0$ or $x=-2$, i.e. the points $(0,0)$ and $(-2,-4)$.

On $[-2,0]$, $-x^{2}\geq 2x$ (at $x=-1$: $-1>-2$).

$A=\int\limits _{-2}^{0}\left (-x^{2}-2x\right )dx=\left [-\frac{x^{3}}{3}-x^{2}\right ]_{-2}^{0}=0-\left (\frac{8}{3}-4\right )=\frac{4}{3}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: 60 words can be made using all the letters of the word $\mathrm{BHBJO}$, with or without meaning. If these words are written as in a dictionary, then the $50^{\text{th}}$ word is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the $50^{\text{th}}$ word formed by the letters of "BHBJO" as if listed in a dictionary, let's analyze the arrangement methodically. Given the letters are B, H, B, J, O, there are some repetitions with the letter B appearing twice.

First, calculate the total number of permutations of these letters:

$\frac{5!}{2!}=60$

Let's arrange the letters in alphabetical order first: B, B, H, J, O.

We need to systematically count the words while following dictionary order:

1. Words starting with B:

Next position letters: B, H, J, O

Number of permutations: $\frac{4!}{1!}=24$ words

Since 24 words starting with 'B' exist and are less than 50, Move to next starting letter alphabetically.

2. Words starting with H:

Next position letters: B, B, J, O

Number of permutations: $\frac{4!}{2!}=12$ words

After 'B', tally becomes 24 (B-words) + 12 (H-words) = 36, needs more.

3. Words starting with J:

Next position letters: B, B, H, O

Number of permutations: $\frac{4!}{2!}=12$ words

Now tally is 36 + 12 = 48 words.

Still 2 more to reach 50.

4. Words starting with O:

Next position letters: B, B, H, J

Number of permutations: $\frac{4!}{2!}=12$ words

Our answer must be here since 48 + 2 more = 50 total.

First permutation: $OBBHJ$

Second permutation (50th word): $OBBJH$

So, the $50^{\text{th}}$ word is: OBBJH

Thus, the correct answer is Option A: OBBJH.

text: Consider three vectors $⃗{a},⃗{b},⃗{c}$. Let $|⃗{a}|=2,|⃗{b}|=3$ and $⃗{a}=⃗{b}\times ⃗{c}$. If $α\in \left [0,\frac{π}{3}\right ]$ is the angle between the vectors $⃗{b}$ and $⃗{c}$, then the minimum value of $27|⃗{c}-⃗{a}|^{2}$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} ⃗{a}=⃗{b}\times ⃗{c} \\ |⃗{a}|=2,|⃗{b}|=3 \end{array}$

$⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b}=0$ and $⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}=0$

$\begin{array}{l} |⃗{c}-⃗{a}|^{2}=|⃗{c}|^{2}+|⃗{a}|^{2}-2⃗{c}\cdot ⃗{a} \\ =4+|⃗{c}|^{2} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} |⃗{a}|=|⃗{b}\times ⃗{c}|=|⃗{b}|\sin α|⃗{c}| \\ \Rightarrow \sin α|⃗{c}|=\dfrac{2}{3} \\ \Rightarrow \sin ^{2}α=\dfrac{4}{9|⃗{c}|^{2}} \\ \Rightarrow |⃗{c}|^{2}=\dfrac{4}{9\sin ^{2}α} \\ \Rightarrow |⃗{c}-⃗{a}|^{2}=4+\dfrac{4}{9\sin ^{2}α} \end{array}$

For $|⃗{c}-⃗{a}|^{2}$ to be minimum for $α\in \left [0,\frac{π}{3}\right ]$

$\begin{array}{l} \sin α=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ 27|⃗{c}-⃗{a}|^{2}=27\left [4+\dfrac{4\cdot 4}{9\cdot 3}\right ] \\ =27\left [\dfrac{124}{27}\right ]=124 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift

text: The differential equation of the family of circles passing through the origin and having centre at the line $y=x$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Equation of circle passing through origin & having centre at the line $y=x$ is


[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} (x-t)^{2}+(y-t)^{2}=2t^{2} \\ x^{2}+y^{2}+t^{2}+t^{2}-2tx-2ty=2t^{2} \\ x^{2}+y^{2}=2t(x+y) \end{array}$

Now differentiate

$\begin{array}{l} 2x+2yy^{'}=2t\left (1+y^{'}\right ) \\ t=\dfrac{x+yy^{'}}{1+y^{'}} \end{array}$

Now, $x^{2}+y^{2}=2\left (\frac{x+yy^{'}}{1+y^{'}}\right )(x+y)$

$\begin{array}{l} x^{2}+y^{2}+x^{2}\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y^{2}\dfrac{dy}{dx} \\ =2\left (x^{2}+xy+xy\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y^{2}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right ) \\ dx\left (x^{2}+y^{2}-2x^{2}-2xy\right )=dy\left (2xy+2y^{2}-x^{2}-y^{2}\right ) \\ dx\left (x^{2}-y^{2}+2xy\right )=dy\left (x^{2}-y^{2}-2xy\right ) \end{array}$

text:
Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation

$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}+\frac{2x}{(1+x^{2})^{2}}y=x\mathrm{e}^{\frac{1}{\left (1+x2\right )}};y(0)=0.$

Then the area enclosed by the curve $f(x)=y(x)\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{1}{\left (1+x2\right )}}$ and the line $y-x=4$ is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{2x}{(1+x^{2})^{2}}y=xe^{\frac{1}{1+x2}};y(0)=0$

I.F. of linear differential equation,

$\begin{array}{l} \text{I.F.}=e^{\int \frac{2x}{\left (1+x2\right )2}}dx=e^{\left (\frac{-1}{1+x2}\right )} \\ \Rightarrow y\left (e^{\left (\frac{-1}{1+x2}\right )}\right )=\int x\cdot e^{\frac{1}{1+x2}}\cdot e^{\left (\frac{-1}{1+x2}\right )}dx \\ =\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}+c \\ \Rightarrow y(0)=0\Rightarrow 0\left (e^{-1}\right )=c\Rightarrow c=0 \\ \Rightarrow y=\dfrac{e^{\frac{1}{1+x2}}\cdot x^{2}}{2} \end{array}$

Area between curve $ye^{\left (\frac{-1}{1+x2}\right )}=\frac{x^{2}}{2}$ and $y-x=4$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 2(x+4)=x^{2}\Rightarrow x^{2}-2x-8=0 \\ \Rightarrow (x-4)(x+2)=0 \\ \int\limits _{-2}^{4}\left [(x+4)-\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right ]dx=\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}+4x-\dfrac{x^{3}}{6}\left |_{-2}^{4} \\ =\left (8+16-\dfrac{64}{6}\right )-\left (2-8+\dfrac{8}{6}\right ) \\ =30-12=18 \end{array} \right.$

text:
Let the mean and the standard deviation of the probability distribution

  
    $\mathrm{X}$

be $μ$ and $σ$, respectively. If $σ-μ=2$, then $σ+μ$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mean $(μ)=\Sigma x_{i}P(x_{i})$

Standard deviation $(σ)=\sqrt{\left (\Sigma x_{i}^{2}P(x_{i})\right )-μ^{2}}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow μ=\dfrac{1}{3}α+K-\dfrac{3}{4} \\ σ=\sqrt{\left (\dfrac{1}{3}α^{2}+K+0+\dfrac{9}{4}\right )-\left (\dfrac{1}{3}α+K-\dfrac{3}{4}\right )^{2}} \\ \because \Sigma P_{i}=1\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{3}+K+\dfrac{1}{6}+\dfrac{1}{4}=1 \\ \Rightarrow K=\dfrac{1}{4}\Rightarrow μ=\dfrac{1}{3}α-\dfrac{1}{2} \\ \because σ-μ=2 \\ σ^{2}=(μ+2)^{2} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{1}{3}α^{2}+\dfrac{5}{2}-μ^{2}=(μ+2)^{2} \\ \dfrac{1}{3}α^{2}+\dfrac{5}{2}=\left (\dfrac{1}{3}α-\dfrac{1}{2}\right )^{2}+\left (\dfrac{1}{3}α+\dfrac{3}{2}\right )^{2} \\ \Rightarrow α=0,6 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \text{If}α=0,K=\frac{1}{4} & \text{If}α=6,K=\frac{1}{4} \\ μ=-\frac{1}{2},σ=\frac{3}{2} & μ=\frac{3}{2},σ=\frac{7}{2} \\ σ+μ=1 & σ+μ=5 \end{array}$

Both (1) and (5) are correct but according to NTA
(5) is correct

text: If $1+\frac{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{3}}+\frac{5-2\sqrt{6}}{18}+\frac{9\sqrt{3}-11\sqrt{2}}{36\sqrt{3}}+\frac{49-20\sqrt{6}}{180}+\ldots$ upto $\infty =2+\left (\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}+1\right )\log _{e}\left (\frac{a}{b}\right )$, where a and b are integers with $\gcd (a,b)=1$, then $11\mathrm{a}+18\mathrm{b}$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} S=1+\dfrac{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{3}}+\dfrac{5-2\sqrt{6}}{18}+\dfrac{9\sqrt{3}-11\sqrt{2}}{36\sqrt{3}}+\ldots \infty  \\  \\ =1+\dfrac{(1-\sqrt{2}/\sqrt{3})}{2}+\dfrac{(1-\sqrt{2}/\sqrt{3})^{2}}{6}+\dfrac{(1-\sqrt{2}/\sqrt{3})^{3}}{12}+\ldots \infty  \end{array}$

$\text{let}1-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}=a$

$\begin{array}{l} S=1+\dfrac{a}{2}+\dfrac{a^{2}}{6}+\dfrac{a^{3}}{12}+\ldots  \\  \\ =1+\left (1-\dfrac{1}{2}\right )a+\left (\dfrac{1}{2}-\dfrac{1}{3}\right )a^{2}+\left (\dfrac{1}{3}-\dfrac{1}{4}\right )a^{3}+\ldots  \\  \\ =1+\left (a+\dfrac{a^{2}}{2}+\dfrac{a^{3}}{3}\ldots \infty \right )+\dfrac{1}{a}\left (\dfrac{-a^{2}}{2}-\dfrac{a^{3}}{3}-\dfrac{a^{4}}{4}\ldots \infty \right ) \\  \\ =-\ln (1-a)+\dfrac{1}{a}\left (-a-\dfrac{a^{2}}{2}-\dfrac{a^{3}}{3}\ldots \infty \right )+2 \\  \\ =-\ln (1-a)+\dfrac{1}{a}\ln (1-a)+2 \\  \\ =2+\left (\dfrac{1}{a}-1\right )\ln (1-a) \\  \\ =2+\left (\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2}}-1\right )\ln \left (1-1+\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}\right ) \\  \\ =2+\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2}}\ln \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}} \\  \\ =2+\left (\dfrac{\sqrt{6}+2}{1}\cdot \dfrac{1}{2}\ln \dfrac{2}{3}\right ) \\  \\ \therefore 2+\left (\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}+1\right )\ln \dfrac{2}{3} \\  \\ \therefore 11a+18b=76 \end{array}$

text: Let $\mathrm{a}>0$ be a root of the equation $2x^{2}+x-2=0$. If $\lim _{x\to \frac{1}{a}}\frac{16\left (1-\cos \left (2+x-2x^{2}\right )\right )}{(1-ax)^{2}}=α+β\sqrt{17}$, where $α,β\in Z$, then $α+β$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $a>0$ is a root of $2x^{2}+x-2=0$, $a=\dfrac{\sqrt{17}-1}{4}$ and $\dfrac{1}{a}=\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{17}-1}=\dfrac{\sqrt{17}+1}{4}$.

Dividing $2a^{2}+a-2=0$ by $a^{2}$ gives $2+\dfrac{1}{a}-\dfrac{2}{a^{2}}=0$, so $x=\dfrac{1}{a}$ is a root of $2+x-2x^{2}=0$. The other root is $\dfrac{1}{2}-\dfrac{1}{a}=\dfrac{1-\sqrt{17}}{4}$, so

$2+x-2x^{2}=-2\left (x-\frac{1}{a}\right )\left (x-\frac{1-\sqrt{17}}{4}\right ).$

Let $u=2+x-2x^{2}$; then $u\to 0$ as $x\to \dfrac{1}{a}$ and $\dfrac{1-\cos u}{u^{2}}\to \dfrac{1}{2}$, so the limit equals $\lim _{x\to 1/a}8\left (\dfrac{u}{1-ax}\right )^{2}$.

Since $1-ax=-a\left (x-\dfrac{1}{a}\right )$,

$\frac{u}{1-ax}=\frac{2}{a}\left (x-\frac{1-\sqrt{17}}{4}\right )\to \frac{2}{a}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{17}}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{17}(\sqrt{17}+1)}{4}=\frac{17+\sqrt{17}}{4}.$

Therefore the limit is $8\cdot \dfrac{(17+\sqrt{17})^{2}}{16}=\dfrac{306+34\sqrt{17}}{2}=153+17\sqrt{17}$.

So $α=153$, $β=17$ and $α+β=170$.

Hence, the answer is 170.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift

text: If $f(t)=\int\limits _{0}^{π}\frac{2x\mathrm{d}x}{1-\cos ^{2}\mathrm{t}\sin ^{2}x},0<\mathrm{t}<π$, then the value of $\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{π^{2}\mathrm{dt}}{f(\mathrm{t})}$ equals $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} f(t)=\int\limits _{0}^{π}\dfrac{2xdx}{1-\cos ^{2}t\sin ^{2}x} \\ x\to π-x \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} f(t)=\int\limits _{0}^{π}\dfrac{2(π-x)dx}{1-\cos ^{2}t\sin ^{2}x}=2π\int\limits _{0}^{π}\dfrac{dx}{1-\cos ^{2}t\sin ^{2}x}-f(t) \\ \Rightarrow f(t)=π\int\limits _{0}^{π}\dfrac{dx}{1-\cos ^{2}t\sin ^{2}x} \\ =2π\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\dfrac{dx}{1-\cos ^{2}t\sin ^{2}x} \\ f(t)=2π\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\dfrac{\sec ^{2}xdx}{\sec ^{2}x-\cos ^{2}t\tan ^{2}x} \\ I_{1}=\int \dfrac{\sec ^{2}xdx}{\sec ^{2}x-\cos ^{2}t\tan ^{2}x} \\ \text{Put}\cos t\tan x=λ\Rightarrow \cos t\sec ^{2}xdx=dλ \\ I_{1}=\int \dfrac{dλ}{\cos t\cdot (1+λ^{2}\sec ^{2}t-λ^{2})}=\int \dfrac{dλ}{\cos t\left (1+λ^{2}\tan ^{2}t\right )} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll} =\dfrac{1}{\cos t\cdot \tan ^{2}t}\cdot \int \dfrac{dλ}{λ^{2}+\cot ^{2}t}= & \dfrac{1}{\cos t\tan ^{2}t} \\ \times \dfrac{1}{\cot t}\tan ^{-1}(λ\tan t) \end{array}$

$\left. \begin{array}{ll} \quad =\dfrac{1}{\sin t}\tan ^{-1}(\sin t\tan x) \\ \Rightarrow  & f(t)=\dfrac{2π}{\sin t}\tan ^{-1}(\sin t\tan x)\right ]_{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}=\dfrac{π^{2}}{\sin t} \\ \Rightarrow  & \int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\dfrac{π^{2}dt}{f(t)}=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\sin tdt=1 \end{array}$

text: Let a line perpendicular to the line $2x-y=10$ touch the parabola $y^{2}=4(x-9)$ at the point P. The distance of the point P from the centre of the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}-14x-8y+56=0$ is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 5th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Line perpendicular to $2x-y=10$ have slope $=\frac{-1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ Line tangent to parabola $y^{2}=4(x-9)$ with slope $m$ is

$\begin{array}{l} y=m(x-9)+\dfrac{1}{m},m=\dfrac{-1}{2} \\ \Rightarrow y=\dfrac{-(x-9)}{2}-2\Rightarrow 2y=-x+9-4 \\ \Rightarrow 2y+x=5 \end{array}$

Solving the tangent and parabola we get point $P$

$\begin{array}{l} \left (\dfrac{5-x}{2}\right )^{2}=4(x-9)\Rightarrow x^{2}-10x+25=16x-144 \\ \Rightarrow x^{2}-26x+169=0\Rightarrow (x-13)^{2}=0 \\ \Rightarrow P\equiv (13,-4) \end{array}$

Distance of $P$ from the centre of circle $(7,4)$ is $\sqrt{(13-7)^{2}+(-4-4)^{2}}=\sqrt{36+64}=10$ units.
